candidates.name: dr-tourism-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Single-file static HTML dashboard (index.html, ~37KB, one commit, updated 2026-05-30) with embedded (hand-entered, not linked raw files) Dominican Republic tourism series 2019-2025: total visitor arrivals (6.4M in 2019 to 12.5M 2025e), air arrivals, cruise passengers (1.1M to 2.65M), tourism revenue in USD ($7.5B to $10.9B), tourism as % of GDP (8.1% to 8.8%), 2024 airport-level passenger counts (Punta Cana 9.55M, Las Americas 5.48M, Cibao 2.29M, Puerto Plata with 2021-2024 breakdown), 2024 source-market shares (USA 50%, Canada 12%, Panama 6%, Colombia 5%, Puerto Rico 5%), and hotel room capacity (87,322 rooms, 10,060 pipeline). Footer cites sources: MITUR, JAC, Banco Central (BCRD), ASONAHORES, UN Tourism.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU, specifically Caribbean/LatAm) with a compact, already-aggregated annual DR tourism series through 2024/2025 sourced from BCRD/MITUR — useful as a cross-check series or to locate the underlying BCRD/MITUR releases, though the repo itself is a single static page with numbers baked into HTML, not a machine-readable table, and it is a personal project (0 stars) so the figures are unverified against source.

candidates.name: gowalla-dataset-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Notebook/scripts for handling the Gowalla check-in dataset (Stanford SNAP social/location dataset, ~196K users, ~6.4M worldwide geotagged check-ins, 2009-2010). Repo processes the public dataset rather than shipping tourism-specific extracts; global coverage includes some Caribbean/Central American points of interest but they are not isolated.
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap #20 (geotagged tourism datasets: Foursquare/Gowalla check-ins) as a worked example of loading/parsing the Gowalla check-in corpus, which could be re-mined for regional check-in density or trip length-of-stay proxies in island/Caribbean POIs if someone wanted to build that from the raw SNAP file.
candidates.size_hint: SNAP Gowalla dataset (~6.4M check-ins) referenced, repo itself is code

candidates.name: gowalla-exp
candidates.what_it_holds: Trajectory-based analysis/experiment code over the same public Gowalla check-in dataset (worldwide geotagged social check-ins, 2009-2010).
candidates.why_useful: Same rationale as gowalla-dataset-analysis: a second, slightly more developed (trajectory modeling) code path onto the Gowalla check-in corpus relevant to gap #20's geotagged mobility datasets; not island/Caribbean specific and needs substantial rework to extract a tourism-relevant series.

candidates.name: foursquare-exp
candidates.what_it_holds: Trajectory-based experiments using the public Foursquare check-in dataset (geotagged venue check-ins).
candidates.why_useful: Also matches gap #20's explicit mention of Foursquare check-in data as a party-size/travel-flow proxy source; global not Caribbean-specific, and is old/lightly maintained (2 stars, last touched 2015).
candidates.time_coverage: circa 2012-2014 Foursquare check-ins (dataset vintage, not repo commit date)

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: exhaustive gh search repos queries across Caribbean Tourism Organization (CTO), Costa Rica ICT, Dominican Republic BCRD/MITUR, Bahamas, Puerto Rico, Jamaica, Aruba, and generic 'caribbean tourism statistics'/'STR caribbean hotel data'/'visitor arrivals dataset caribbean' phrasing returned almost entirely empty result sets or irrelevant tourist-facing apps (e.g. Aruba tourism guide app = a consumer app, no stats). No repo mirrors official CTO, Costa Rica ICT, Bahamas MOTIA, or Puerto Rico Tourism Company statistical releases, and no Hawaii-DBEDT-style party-size/length-of-stay survey repo exists for any Caribbean/Central American country. The one real find (dr-tourism-dashboard) is a single hobbyist HTML page with hand-entered annual DR figures, not a structured dataset or pull script — still worth flagging since it is genuinely new data (BCRD/MITUR sourced, not already held) and points to the underlying official sources (MITUR, JAC, Banco Central RD, ASONAHORES) that a human could pull directly instead of via GitHub. Also flagged the Gowalla/Foursquare check-in repos since gap #20 explicitly names those datasets, but they are generic global ML repos, not Caribbean-tailored. Hit the GitHub search API rate limit twice (403) mid-run; recovered after a documented 40s wait via Monitor (Start-Sleep was blocked as a standalone tool call in this environment) and one retry as instructed. Also exhausted the session's WebSearch budget after one query, so could not cross-check via general web search beyond WebFetch on specific candidate URLs. Recommendation for a future scout: rather than more gh search repos passes (this theme appears to have been searched close to exhaustively), try `gh search code` (sparingly, 10/min cap) for filenames like 'ICT_estadisticas' or 'BCRD_turismo' or check whether CTO/Costa Rica ICT publish anything on data.gov-style CKAN/Socrata portals that a generic 'ckan client caribbean' or 'socrata tourism' gh search might surface as an acquisition-method repo instead of a stored dataset.
